title: the Ninefold Court Rising Revisited
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse on the night the stars vanish, Lior Oyelaran discovers her homeland has been erased from the world's memory — its people scattered, its Ninefold Court dissolved a century ago by an oath her own blood helped swear. Guided by a disgraced court archivist, a child who remembers the erased country, and the ghost of her oath-bound grandmother, Lior follows the smugglers' roads inward to the buried throne room where the Court's nine seats wait. To restore Thornfell she must break her family's founding oath — but the usurper who unmade the country offers her inheritance instead: a throne built on forgetting. Lior chooses justice outside the law, reforges the Ninefold Court from the scattered and dispossessed rather than the noble-born, and speaks the stars back into the sky at the cost of her own name in the world's memory.
about_author: Mara Delacroix is the pen name of a former border-region cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes that no longer appear on official charts. Her fiction blends smuggler's-road pragmatism with a cartographer's love for countries that exist only in memory.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Guiding a smuggler's caravan through Thornfell's high passes, Lior watches the border wards shatter and the stars vanish overhead in the same breath. The caravan scatters; her compass spins uselessly. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a guide whose maps have suddenly lied to her.

chapters.title: A Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Descending into the valley town of Emberhold, she finds its people alive but unable to name their own nation; records burn cold to her touch. Only her oath-bound blood lets her perceive what was erased. Beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Vale, a court archivist who helped catalog the erasure and regrets it, intercepts Lior and reveals the Ninefold Court was dissolved by oath, not conquest. Beat: uneasy alliance between guilt and anger.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In Emberhold's orphanage, Lior meets Sefi, a girl who hums the erased anthem and draws the nine seats from dreams. The usurper's grey-cloaked Wardens arrive hunting her. Beat: found family's first spark, and first blood.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads Inward
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior leads her ragged company through unwarded passes only she knows, evading Warden patrols. Wren teaches Sefi the Court's old law; Lior pretends not to care. Beat: the road becoming a home.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Ghost
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At a wayside shrine, the ghost of oath-speaker Adaeze Oyelaran manifests, bound to the founding oath that erased Thornfell. She warns Lior that breaking it will unmake the Oyelaran name. Beat: inheritance revealed as a cage.

chapters.title: Nine Empty Seats
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The company reaches the buried throne hall beneath the mountains and finds nine stone seats, each holding a fragment of the old Court's power. Wren confesses he catalogued this room. Beat: awe curdled with shame.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Offer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Regent of Ash — the man who unmade the country — appears not as a tyrant but as a tired official, offering Lior a restored throne if she inherits the forgetting as her family did. Beat: temptation with a reasonable face.

chapters.title: What the Oath Bought
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV (ghost chapters). The ghost recounts the famine century ago when the nine houses swore to dissolve the Court and feed the people by erasing the wars with them. Beat: sympathy for the sin Lior must undo.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Ford
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Wardens ambush the company at a river ford; Sefi's memory of the old country proves to be a weapon — her spoken names burn the erasure off soldiers' minds. Beat: the child becomes the heart of the cause.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Rescued soldiers, remembering Thornfell, are hunted by their own former comrades. Lior must choose to shelter them, burning her last safe route out. Beat: justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: A Court of Strays
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In an abandoned mine, the company shelters dozens of the remembering. Wren proposes reforging the Court not with noble blood but with smugglers, soldiers, orphans. Beat: the theme of inheritance rewritten.

chapters.title: The Regent's Mercy
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Regent captures Sefi but releases her unharmed with a message: the forgetting protects Thornfell's people from a war the world wants to resume. Beat: doubt at its deepest.

chapters.title: The World Outside the Wards
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren slips beyond the fallen border and finds neighboring kingdoms massing to carve up the vanished land — proof the erasure was a dam against conquest. Beat: the enemy's argument gains weight.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Broken Seat
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. The ghost reveals her seat among the nine was the first to swear and the first to regret; her fragment of power can anchor a new oath — if Lior can forgive her. Beat: reconciliation with the ancestor.

chapters.title: The Siege of Emberhold
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Wardens burn Emberhold to erase the remembering; the strays defend the town with Sefi's names and Lior's swordwork. They win the street but lose the archive. Beat: fury transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Second Oath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the mine, Wren drafts the Second Oath: a Ninefold Court seated by service, not blood, with a clause to release the Oyelaran line. Lior refuses to sign away her name's burden alone. Beat: solidarity over sacrifice.

chapters.title: March of the Remembering
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Hundreds of the remembering march openly on the buried throne hall, singing the erased anthem as Wardens falter, their own erased memories stirring. Beat: hope made loud and dangerous.

chapters.title: The Throne Hall Stand
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Regent makes his last stand in the throne hall, revealing he was the ninth oath-speaker's heir, keeping the forgetting alive out of the same love that built it. Beat: enemy and hero mirror each other.

chapters.title: Breaking the Founding Oath
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax. Lior speaks the counter-oath, shattering the founding vow; Adaeze's ghost spends herself anchoring it; the stars begin to bleed back through the dark. Beat: grief and triumph in one breath.

chapters.title: The Ninefold Court Rising
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The nine seats fill with a smuggler, a soldier, an orphan, an archivist, and others; the Regent, defeated, takes a seat of penance. Thornfell's borders reweave — but Lior's name is fading from memory. Beat: the cost comes due.

chapters.title: The Nameless Guide
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Resolution. No chart remembers Lior Oyelaran, yet every road does; Sefi, now the Court's youngest speaker, keeps her memory alive by telling her story aloud. Lior walks the passes again, unknown and free. Beat: inheritance fulfilled by release.
